mission_06: Noise robustness is essential for speech recognition systems deployed in real-world environments where background noise, reverberation, and interference degrade recognition accuracy. Spectral subtraction is one of the oldest and simplest noise reduction techniques, estimating the noise spectrum during silent periods and subtracting it from the noisy speech spectrum. The oversubtraction factor alpha controls how aggressively noise is removed, while the spectral floor beta prevents negative values that cause musical noise artifacts. The Wiener filter provides an optimal linear filter in the mean-square error sense, computing a frequency-dependent gain that balances noise suppression against speech distortion based on the signal-to-noise ratio at each frequency bin. Spectral gating applies a hard or soft threshold to the STFT magnitude, zeroing out components below a noise floor. Data augmentation with noise at various SNR levels during training is another powerful approach, teaching the model to be invariant to noise conditions. In this mission, you will implement spectral subtraction, Wiener filtering, spectral gating, noise addition at controlled SNR levels, and SNR improvement evaluation, building a comprehensive noise robustness toolkit.
